comments.comment: Session 11 built the team communication architecture on Session 3's section 11 as asked. Non-co-presence by hour is the architecture's first premise, the four tests survive with accessibility read per language on every surface, and the three channels are made provable by a change-reach record the stack writes from records that exist: a change has reached the house when every open period's brief since its version marks the change line and the team home shows it in every house language, and has reached a person when their check-in dates after the version. The house's languages are a versioned list from the seat sheets' field 14 and the roster's chosen languages, every house-written surface exists in every listed language under one version number before it publishes, the brief runs in tonight's roster's languages by the block on the surface and an interpreter designation, and a person's own words are never translated for the house. The transparency line is closed by the team for everything that is not an operating figure, individual review content beyond the person and their lead, or the financial model (shared at the moment it is versioned, to every period at once, in every house language), and the rest stays on `86akh5uby`. S11 page, sections 4, 7, 8, and 13; P9, P15 to P19, P32, P33.

Session 11 designed the communication system the cadence artifacts run on. Every artifact reaches the house through the three channels proven by the change-reach record, the cadence page and every other team home page exist in every language on the house's list under one version number with a translation record naming translator and approvers, and the language list itself is a versioned definitions entry the Operations Lead holds. The transparency line at the leads' review record, the house review notes, and the goal pages is closed for everything that is not a lagging figure, individual review content beyond the person and their lead, or the financial model: those publish to the team home at the moment they are versioned, minus figure lines and person items, in every house language; the figures and the review content stay founder-gated on `86akh5uby`. S11 page, sections 7, 8, and 13; P15 to P19, P32, P33.

Session 11 developed the composition position to the ceiling the record allows. The team drafts and marks recommended a statement about the house's conduct, every sentence of which is a rule the record or a prior session holds: four reads and nothing about who a person is; every stage in the chosen language; nothing about who a person is on any record about them beyond the seat's language field; the house reads its own reach and widens it when it narrows, moving no bar; no target for the composition of the team, stated so no one is read against one, which the four reads and the person page's refusals entail. Once the statement exists, Session 5's source-dominance and stage-rate read acts, on the house's reach (the sheet's sourcing mix, the process languages, the board's placement) and the process (the calibration read's note, module, and anchor proposal), never on a candidate, a scorecard, or a bar, and never slowing a seat for a pipeline's shape. Whether the house states anything about who it hopes its team will be beyond that conduct statement is a values statement the founders make; three options are argued and the team recommends stating nothing beyond conduct, noting that a statement about reach in the record's terms is available without a new read. Self-identification is the founders' with counsel; the team recommends declining for now. S11 page, section 15; P35 to P38. Filed as work item A5 and extended on `86akh7r8z`.

Session 11 read canon's register for employee-facing surfaces and marked it held on the same question as Session 5's candidate-facing reading, for canon's owner as one ruling (`86akh7r2t`): a house-written internal page is correspondence's cousin with "we" as the house and "you" to the person, every sentence under the six binary tests with the competitor test as the working one; the brief is speech reading a record's words; the check-in is a conversation canon does not script; a person's own words carry the language constant and nothing else of canon's, held with Session 10's finding 20.10. The language obligations are made one system: the house's language list is the union of field 14 across every open sheet plus every roster member's chosen language, every house-written surface exists in every listed language before it publishes, the brief runs in tonight's roster's languages by the block on the surface and an interpreter designation, translation is paid work with two approvals under one version number, and canon's Korean terms stand untranslated in every version with the question whether an internal page is a brand context filed as one question with the candidate's. S11 page, sections 8 and 9; P17 to P19, P23, P24.

Session 11 stated bias measurement's data in the diagnostic's form. What: the source tag, the pool tag, the chosen interview language and format, each stage's outcome in the four states, the on-sheet decline reason, the interviewer, and the dates, per seat and per stage, from records Session 5 already specified in Greenhouse and nothing added. Read by whom and when: the leads' review weekly for source dominance and stage rate; the calibration read monthly (the Maitre d, pre-opening the calibrating partner); the ninety-day outcome read per hire; the whole record at the reset with the dominance count as a parameter. Refusals: no target, no figure, no significance claim, no name, no inferred attribute, no act on a candidate, a scorecard, a decision, or a bar, no seat slowed. Whether the house asks candidates for self-identification is the founders' with counsel: if asked, voluntary, after the packet, invisible to every assessor, decider, lead, and mentor, read in aggregate for the reach question only, never joined to a person page, its form and retention counsel's; the team recommends declining for now because the reach read acts without it. S11 page, sections 15.5 and 16; P37, P39. Extends `86akh9tbd`.

Session 11's inclusion and communication work inherited the mechanism and the hold and generalized both. The interpreter at the why block becomes the interpreter designation, named at the brief beside the room, the door, the sequence, and the pass for any roster language the room's owner does not hold, on the clock, rotating under the floor, speaking the readiness block, the change line, and a recognition in that language, writing nothing, never customer-facing; a check-in run through it is founder-gated because it changes who is in the room. Every module, page, and brief exists in every language on the house's list, which is a versioned definitions entry; a page in one language when the list has two has not been published. The module standard's hold on glossing a Korean term is carried to every internal page: canon's terms stand untranslated in every language version, an internal page says what a term asks of a seat without defining it, and whether an internal page is a brand context is filed as one question with the candidate's for canon's owner (`86akh7r2t`, `86akhb2jv`). Finding 18.4's shape recurs one step later: the pre-opening translators are the founders and the first leads, and their languages are a critical-path fact on the hiring calendar. S11 page, section 8; P17 to P21.

Session 11 took all four halves. Crisis inward: a live risk reaches the house in two ways only, as a change line item with the record's three-part reason (what happened, the real impact, the fix or that there is none yet) where it changes what the roster does tonight, and as a versioned statement on the team home in every house language spoken at the next brief where it touches the house whole; otherwise it stays on the partners' page; nothing is said before it is written, and a public statement reaches the team home before or at the moment it publishes. The unblocking practice: either party's duty to write; one joint half-page (the problem as the outcome for the customer or the house, the options, the trade-offs) under the six tests; decided by the range's owner inside one domain, as a Class B hold across domains, as Class C between the leads, never up a line; on the record by the next leads' review and decided with its reason within the loop-closure window; an owner refuses a unilateral case until the absent party has been asked to write. The four-channel order in practice: the stack places the affected person's check-in before the version publishes and the entry waits for it, the person hears the reason as the evidence line's words, the sheet publishes in every house language, every open period's brief speaks one sentence under the change line, the team home shows it, and a change-reach record proves each step. Events: once the founders rule who holds one, its internal telling is the menu turn's through the three channels ahead of first service and its public telling the brand cadence's classes; until then an event is a service on the book and nothing is announced. S11 page, sections 10 and 11; P25, P26, P28, P29.

Session 11 fixed the practice of all three. On a departure the domain lead writes the tension-loss row the day it is known, the leads' review's line follows, the next brief of every open period speaks coverage once under the change line in the roster's languages (which seat is open, which seats hold its functions this service, which designation carries what the node held) and thereafter as the designations' line while the seat is open, the inventory shows the seat open with the pool read recorded, and nothing about the person is said; the departing person's own words are theirs and the house speaks none. The narrowing of Session 3's "announced" to coverage is surfaced for founder ratification beside S3 P11.6 rather than overwritten. The channels' order is read as a count on the change-reach record at the leads' review and the house review: a brief dated before the affected check-in, a period's brief missing the line, a language version lagging, the one thing missing from a period's week, each written as sequence corruption on the entry with the fix on the mechanism and never on the person who did not speak or hold. "Diagnostic" and the modes' names appear only on the leads' review record, the house memo, the reset's record, and the team home's diagnostic page, never in a spoken item at the brief or on a recognition, and the floor's words are coverage, the change line, what the system learned, and the readiness block; readiness row 137 searches for the vocabulary. S11 page, sections 7.3 and 10.2; P16, P25, P27.

Session 11 answered all three. The slot's "what the system learned" and the gathering's "what the house learned" are process and never a person or a figure, so both fall inside the part of the transparency line the team closes (shared at the moment it is versioned, to every period, in every house language) and neither is governed by the founder-gated line; the destinations page exists in every house language before the first cohort's why block because it is delivered there, and the architecture page is its parent. The Thursday hour's paragraph changes nothing: its personal round is the vulnerability prompt Session 10 refused and its topic list is the leads' review's fixed agenda derived from the closes and the lead's note; the leads have no second meeting and the partners' creator hour is the pre-opening review and the annual block; the quarterly offsite is answered by S10 P17. Finding 20.10: Session 11 holds Session 10's reading that the language constant applies to a peer's words and the lexicon does not, extends it to the check-in line, the capture's free field, and a channel item, and adds that the house-written parts of the same surfaces carry canon in full; it files a sibling finding that canon splits speech from writing once and the brief is speech reading a record, so a peer's word spoken by the room's owner is a change of speaker canon's owner must rule on. S11 page, sections 2, 9.2, 13.2; P2, P24, P32.

Session 11 split the question. The part the record entails is drafted and marked recommended as a statement about the house's conduct (four reads and nothing about who a person is; every stage in the chosen language; nothing about who a person is on any record about them; the house reads and widens its own reach and moves no bar; no target, stated so no one is read against one), filed as work item A5 for ratification. The part that is a values statement stays here: whether the house says anything about who it hopes its team will be beyond conduct. Three options argued on the page: state nothing beyond conduct (recommended, because a position the house cannot read without breaking its own rules is a sentence and not a mechanism); state an aspiration in the record's terms, that the house's reach is as wide as its customers' door, which is readable and adds one sentence and no read; state an aspiration in her terms, which is unreadable at the house's volume without a self-identification record and the team does not draft. Finding 20.9 is the record's own tension: it reads its customers' demographic composition at the door and holds no read of its team's. The founders decide, with counsel; the reach read acts either way. S11 page, section 15.6; P38.

Session 11 answered what the data is (the source tag, pool tag, chosen language and format, stage outcomes, on-sheet decline reasons, interviewer, dates, per seat and stage, from Session 5's records), who reads it and when (the leads' review weekly, the calibration read monthly, the ninety-day read, the reset), and its refusals (no target, figure, significance claim, name, inference, or act on a candidate). What remains for the founders is self-identification: if asked, voluntary, after the packet, invisible to every assessor, decider, lead, and mentor, aggregate only for the reach question, never joined to a person page, its form and retention counsel's; the team recommends declining for now. S11 page, sections 15.5 and 16; P37, P39.

Session 11 closed the part of the line the team has standing to close: everything that is not an operating figure, individual review content beyond the person and their lead, or the financial model is shared at the moment it is versioned, to every open period at once, with every team member, on the team home, in every house language; that includes every versioned decision and its reason, the goal pages' states, the register, the sheets, the mechanism map, the inventory, the destinations and architecture pages, the leads' review's one thing and its notes minus figure lines and person items, the house review's notes likewise, the slot's and the gathering's "learned" items as process, and any live-risk statement that touches the house. What stays for the founders: which lagging figures, if any, appear on any surface the house reads; review content beyond the person and their lead; the financial model; the third seat's access (`86akh5ucu`). The team's recommendation stands as Session 3 wrote it. S11 page, section 13; P32, P33.

Session 11 names the third seat's access as the one part of the transparency line's founder-gated half that the communication architecture cannot route around: every ratified position publishes to the team home at the moment it is versioned, and whether the chef partner reads them before the seat is filled is the founders'. S11 page, section 13.1; P33.

Session 11 adds the communication architecture's reasons for urgency. A concern about a lead is a person-subject item the feedback channel routes and does not carry, and the destinations page reads "held" for it until this closes, so the one topic with no destination is now visible on a page every team member reads. Every range breach on a room's owner or a publisher in S11 section 17 (a frame added to the one thing, a word about a departed person, a recognition read that fails the rules, a person item published, a unilateral case heard, a lead's repeated part in a change-reach failure) has this ruling as its destination and until then goes to the partners' review as a load reading on the lead. Readiness row 118 fails and the destinations page carries a held entry until it closes. S11 page, sections 6.8, 12.2, 17; P30, P41.

Session 11 adds the employee-facing register as the same ruling. The team reads a house-written internal page as correspondence's cousin with "we" as the house and "you" to the person, every sentence under the six binary tests; the brief as speech reading a record's words; the check-in as a conversation canon does not script; and a person's own words as carrying the language constant only. Whether an internal page is a brand context, which decides whether canon's Korean terms may be said to ask something of a seat without being defined, is the same question Session 5 asked for a candidate's document and Session 7 for a module. One ruling closes all three. S11 page, sections 8.4 and 9; P19, P23, P24; instrument I4.

Session 11 carries the module standard's hold to every internal page in every language version: canon's terms stand untranslated, an internal page says what a term asks of a seat without defining it, and a person who does not hold Korean meets the term in person at the why block and from the mentor. Session 11 also finds that the two canon versions list different term sets (Canon 1.0 section 09 names fifteen; Deck 3.0 p.56 names seven) and uses the longer list until `86akh3tjb` reconciles them. S11 page, section 8.4; finding 20.12; P19.

Session 11 files the sibling question as work item A6: whether a synthesized voice answering the house's phone is inside Jaeyeonmi's concealment prohibition, since canon's AI rule names imagery only and Session 7 held Synthesia on the concealment clause. The two are one clause read for two media and should be ruled together. Session 11 also reads a software-drafted translation of an internal page as permitted under canon's disclosure convention once a holder of the language has read it, as the team's reading. S11 page, sections 6.9 and 8.4; finding 20.5; P14, P19.

Session 11 routes four rulings to canon's owner, whoever this names: the internal register (`86akh7r2t`), the synthesized voice on the phone (A6), the Korean terms on internal pages and the two term lists (`86akhb2jv`, `86akh3tjb`), and whether a peer's words on a house surface are a brand surface (S10 finding 20.10, extended to the check-in line, the capture, and a channel item). The first is needed before the first team home page publishes in the team's languages. S11 page, sections 8, 9, 17.9; P41.

Session 11 adds to the reconciliation list that Canon 1.0's preferred Korean terms (section 09) and Deck 3.0's (p.56) differ, fifteen against seven, which decides which words stand untranslated on every internal page in every language; the internal pages use the longer list until reconciled. S11 page, section 8.4; finding 20.12.

Session 11 names what waits on this: the feedback channel's sync to the leads' review record ("syncs to the execution system," WP p.22), the change-reach record's computation, and the copy of a phone-originated message from the phone's software to the book are each recorded on the partners' page as manual until the hub is confirmed and the mesh carries them. No tool on the S11 page is named as the hub, and none becomes one by implication. S11 page, sections 6.8, 6.9, 7.1; P13, P15.

Session 11 places the team home, the person page, the brief's block and record, the close's capture form, and the channel if any on Google Workspace as the interim pending the OS surface, configuration where a page or form serves and a build where the write rules, language versions, record marks, or the capture's time cost cannot be met, and states that the interim is not the decision: every page on the backbone is written to move, and where the team home lives relative to the OS surface inherits this ruling (S3 P11.9). S11 page, sections 6.4 and 6.13; P12.

Session 11 sets the communication rule that waits on this: once ruled, an event's internal telling is the menu turn's, through the three channels ahead of its first service with its own brief under the same spine and its book on the identity spine, and its public telling the brand cadence's classes; until ruled, an event is a service on the book and nothing is announced at a brief. S11 page, section 10.4; P28.

Session 11 adds the same gap one step later: the pre-opening translators of every founding page are the founders and the first leads, so the languages they hold decide whether the first cohort's why block, its destinations page, and its modules exist in the cohort's languages, and a check-in between a person and a lead who share no language needs the interpreter designation the founders must ratify (S11 P20). The founders' languages are named as a critical-path fact on the hiring calendar. S11 page, section 8.5; P20.

Session 11 supplies the practice behind the four channels: the stack places the affected person's check-in before the version publishes and the entry waits for it; the person hears the reason as the evidence line's words and writes their own line; the sheet publishes in every house language and every open candidate is re-read; every open period's brief speaks one sentence under the change line; the team home shows it; a range card's version reaches its holder at the same check-in; and a change-reach record proves each step and is read weekly as counts. S11 page, sections 7 and 10.1; P15, P16, P25.

Session 11 adds the inward rule: a live risk reaches the house in two ways only, as a change line item with the three-part reason where it changes what the roster does tonight, and as a versioned statement on the team home in every house language published no later than the first daily state and spoken at the next brief where it touches the house whole; otherwise it stays on the partners' page; nothing is said before it is written. The inward statement is specified as S11 I11, filed as A26, extending the form here. S11 page, section 10.3; P26.

Session 11 fixes the brief's practice on a departure: coverage once at the next brief of every open period under the change line in the roster's languages, then as the designations' line while the seat is open; the departing person's words are theirs and the house speaks none; the narrowing of S3 P11.6's "announced" is surfaced for ratification beside it. S11 page, section 10.2; P25.

Session 11 supplies the unblocking practice as the form these rules run in: the joint half-page on the leads' review record (Class B) or the partners' page (Class C), either party's duty to write, decided by the range's owner within the loop-closure window, an owner's refusal of a unilateral case until the absent party has been asked to write, and the decision read back on the next scorecard; never up a line.
